title: Effect of physical measures on postoperative swelling: a three-dimensional volumetric analysis
summary: After wrist replacement surgery, the hand, wrist and forearm often swell. This study examines whether additional water cooling with a cooling cuff reduces swelling more than standard aftercare with a splint, elevation and pain treatment. 60 patients are randomly assigned to one of the two groups. Swelling is measured by an assessor unaware of group allocation using a contact-free 3D scanner before surgery and at five time points up to six weeks afterwards. Measurements take place during routine follow-up visits.
conditions: Primary osteoarthritis of other joints: forearm [radius, ulna, wrist]
Post-traumatic osteoarthritis of other joints: forearm [radius, ulna, wrist]

interventions.name: Standard care after total wrist arthroplasty plus continuous postoperative cooling therapy with the Hilotherm® Professional water-cooling system (target temperature 17 °C), applied over the dressing immediately after surgery until discharge (usually 4–5 days).
Standard care after total wrist arthroplasty: volar scaphoid plaster splint, elevation of the operated limb and postoperative analgesia including an axillary plexus catheter.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients undergoing total wrist arthroplasty for degenerative or post-traumatic wrist osteoarthritis; written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
No informed consent; inability or unwillingness to attend follow-up visits; angioedema, lymphoedema or lipoedema.
